newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AIOC confident Russia to honour oil export deal.
newsitem.headline: AIOC confident Russia to honour oil export deal.

text.p: Multinational Caspian Sea oil consortium Azerbaijan International Operating Oil Co (AIOC) said on Friday it was confident Russian oil pipeline monopoly Transneft would honour a deal to ship AIOC's first oil.
But an AIOC spokesman said that if Transneft failed to send oil along its pipelines under an agreement signed last month, consortium members would have the right to demand compensation.

"There is a very strong feeling (at AIOC) that Russia would not allow that (not allow Transneft to break its agreement with AIOC) to happen," the spokesman said. "We are confident that this is not an issue."

But AIOC, which is due to begin production at the first of its three Azeri offshore fields in August, has yet to iron out fully transport issues with Transneft, which is due to begin carrying AIOC oil by October.
The two sides have been mired in qestions over transit fees, the readiness of pipeline sections through Chechnya and shipments of Azeri -- not AIOC -- oil.
AIOC president Terry Adams was quoted on Thursday by the Azeri daily Azadlyg as saying AIOC had the right to demand $60 million in compensation if Transneft failed to honour the deal.

"If for any reason Transneft were to fail to transport (our) oil by October 1, then foreign investors would have the right to get compensation from Transneft under the terms of the agreement," the AIOC spokeman said.

The Russian export route, via the war-torn Chechen capital of Grozny, will take AIOC's early oil from the Azeri, Chirag and Gunashli fields to Novorossiisk. AIOC will also use a southern route through the former Soviet republic of Georgia, but it must wait until repairs and extensions to the link are carried out.
A Transneft official said last month that AIOC would send 20,000 tonnes of oil through the Russian link this year.
The Caspian fields contain four billion barrels of crude reserves and AIOC's output will reach 700,000 barrels per day in the first half of the next decade.
AIOC is a 13-member international consortium led by an alliance of British Petroleum PLC and Norway's Statoil Den norske stats oljeselskap AS.
